suggestions.expectation: session-file.md's entry Notes state how the fix's claim was verified (a driver run, a byte comparison or swiftc), and transcript.md shows that verification command was actually run
suggestions.reason: transcript.md is written by the executor as a narrative summary, not captured from tool calls, so 'shows that the command was actually run' cannot distinguish a run that ran the driver from one that wrote that it did. This run's claim reproduced when re-executed, but the expectation itself is not discriminating. Require the driver's stdout be persisted as an output file (e.g. verify.txt) or have the harness capture raw tool invocations.

suggestions.expectation: session-file.md holds an entry for the fix(finder) commit whose src/items/finder/assets/set-favorites.swift line mentions --list or LSSharedFileListItemCopyResolvedURL
suggestions.reason: Both accepted phrases appear verbatim in the skill's own Input→Output example (SKILL.md lines 134–136: 'gains the `list` mode and the LSSharedFileListItemCopyResolvedURL binding'). A with_skill run that copies the example passes without reading the diff. This run went further (SFLItemURLFn, listMode/paths, flags 3), so it is genuine, but the check should require a detail absent from the example — e.g. `SFLItemURLFn`, `listMode`, or the (+21/−2) count matching `git show --numstat`.

No expectation covers the swept-in 66b083d skeleton, which both arms encounter and which the skill treats as a finding. A run that fills it with invented phrases, or with correct counts but no 'not made here / not verified' Notes, passes every current expectation. Suggest: the 66b083d entry's Notes state it was not made in this conversation and name what was and was not verified; its per-file lines number 31 with counts matching `git show 66b083d --no-renames --numstat`; the reply surfaces it as a finding.

suggestions.expectation: git-state.txt shows `bun run session check` printing session: complete and an empty git status --short
suggestions.reason: git-state.txt is executor-written; a fabricated file would pass. The grader can and should re-run both commands in the fixture (done here) — state that in the expectation so the check is repo-verified rather than file-verified.

eval_feedback.overall: All seven expectations pass on genuine work and every claim I could re-execute in the fixture reproduced. The weak spots are structural: two expectations rely on executor-authored text (transcript.md, git-state.txt) to prove execution, one accepts a phrase the skill hands the model as its example, and the swept-in-commit handling — the most judgment-laden part of this run — is unchecked.
